packets.signature: startMarquee(e) -> void (arms _motionMarquee); applyMarqueeSelection(x0, y0, x1, y1) -> void (DOM-rect coords, mutates DOM .sel classes + selection model via setKeySel); marqueeLayersIn(y0, y1, x0, x1) -> number[] (layer indices swept by the rectangle).
packets.responsibility: _motionMarquee (11925) is the module-level drag-state var, commented with its own shape `{startX, startY, rectEl, moved, layer}`. startMarquee(e) (11926-11935): creates one `.motion-marquee-rect` div appended to `document.body` (11927-11928, NOT inside #frame-grid, so it overlays the whole viewport during the drag); reads, at mousedown time (comment 11929-11931 explains WHY here rather than at mouseup: 'by mouseup the pointer has usually left it'), the `.frow[data-layer]` ancestor of the press target to capture which layer row (if any) was pressed into `_motionMarquee.layer` (11932-11934, null for empty grid space — later read by endMarquee, sibling-covered, as the deselect signal). applyMarqueeSelection(x0,y0,x1,y1) (11936-11957): iterates every `.motion-track-row, .motion-group-row` (11939, a comment at 11938 cites feedback #221, cross-referencing invertKeySelection's identical scan just above in C20p territory), skips untagged rows (`if (!holder) return`, 11941), then for each `.motion-key` diamond inside computes its screen-space center via `getBoundingClientRect()` (11943-11944) and tests it against the caller-supplied rectangle bounds (11945) — geometry is PURELY the rendered diamond's own rect, never frame-index math. `dia.classList.toggle('sel', hit)` (11946) paints the diamond immediately regardless of whether it resolves to a real key. For a hit, it reads `cell.dataset.frame` (11949), calls `trackFor(holder, prop)` (motion.js:443, pre-11412) and `keyAt(track, frame)` (motion.js:1189, pre-11412, binary search for an EXACT frame match) to recover the actual key object, pushing `{holder, prop, key}` (11952) only if `keyAt` found one — a diamond with no backing key (shouldn't normally exist, but the hit-test is purely visual) is silently excluded from the selection while still getting painted '.sel'. `setKeySel(sel)` (11955, motion.js:11473, C20o) is called unconditionally at the end — the comment notes it 'also refreshes the selection box (updateKeySelectionBox below)', i.e. setKeySel's own body (C20o) calls this artifact's own updateKeySelectionBox (packet 3) as part of its selection-model update. Finally, if `_motionMarquee` is still set, `_motionMarquee.layers = marqueeLayersIn(y0,y1,x0,x1)` (11956) — side-channel state for endMarquee's own layer-selection mirror (sibling-covered). marqueeLayersIn(y0,y1,x0,x1) (11975-12000, preceded by a 17-line lead-in 11958-11974 documenting feedback #769 and a 2026-09-03 follow-up in French, both quoted verbatim in the source): walks `#frame-grid`'s DIRECT children in document order (11979-11997), tracking the LAST-seen `.frow[data-layer]` row as `cur`/`curRow` for every subsequent property/element track row that carries no `data-layer` of its own (11981-11985, 'the owning layer is the last .frow[data-layer] seen ABOVE them'); for each candidate row, tests vertical overlap against the swept rect (`b.bottom < y0 || b.top > y1`, 11989) and, if x0/x1 were supplied and the owning row has a rendered `.layer-inout-bar`, ALSO requires horizontal overlap against that BAR's own rect rather than the full-width row (11990-11996, documented at 11966-11972 as a 2026-09-03 fix: a row spans the full timeline width but the visible bar stops at the in/out points, so a rectangle that misses the bar must not select that layer — 'Sans barre rendue (Animation 2D, ligne de propriété), on garde l'ancien comportement: la ligne suffit', i.e. without a rendered bar the plain row-overlap rule still applies). Returns a de-duplicated (`if (out.indexOf(cur) < 0)`, 11997) array of layer indices in first-encountered order.

THIRD guard, the '2+ property tracks' threshold the parent issue asks to confirm (12114-12128, an 8-line lead-in quotes Cyril's own 2026-07-25 feedback verbatim: 'quand on select sur une seule propriété des keyframes pas besoin de la box c'est pour plusieurs keyframes les unes en dessous des autres'): walks the same selected diamonds, collects each one's OWN `.closest('.motion-track-row')` into a de-duplicated `rowsHit` array (12124-12127); if `rowsHit.length < 2` (all selected keys sit on the SAME single track) — remove and bail, with the comment explaining why: skew is undefined on one row (its own handler already refuses under 2 rows) and the box would otherwise just occlude the diamonds and steal their clicks; single-track keys are already draggable as a group by grabbing one. future_proposals.boundary: applyMarqueeSelection today folds 'which keys got selected' and 'which diamonds got painted .sel' into one pass with no return value — a caller that wants to know whether the marquee actually TOUCHED anything (e.g. to skip an unnecessary updateKeySelectionBox re-measure) must re-derive it from `_motionKeySel`'s own length delta rather than reading it off the call itself.

startSkewDrag/onDragMove/onDragUp today communicate purely through the ambient global `window._motionSkewDrag` — documented and functional, but every consumer (this span, C20r's own addSpaceEdges callback, and the drag lifecycle itself) must know that exact global name and shape by convention. A returned handle object would make the coupling explicit and testable without inspecting `window` directly, and would let C20r's own Space-edge reuse (the one gesture it actually shares) be expressed as passing the SAME handle rather than re-deriving fMin/fMax/grabFrame from a second row set.
